title: goal — why we are asking, and what we want to know (4.5.1, 5.1)

purpose.description: Cannot be inferred; a missing purpose is a question for the human (4.5.1)

intent.description: Defaults from purpose. Differing from the default requires intent_rationale (check 32).

targets.description: What accuracy is wanted. In explore mode, stated in decades.

priority.description: Ordered. Safety is deliberately absent: it is a constraint, not a tradeable item (2.1).

compare_variable.description: required when purpose is compare: the one parameter allowed to differ between arms (check 34)

constraint_notes.description: Free-text limits from the human. Named apart from the interval lists elsewhere: same word, different kind of thing.

configuration_preference.description: An ordered tie-break from the person, read by S3.0 ONLY when the cap is unresolved (4.5.1 branch c). It settles which of several capable configurations to spend the fan-out on. It never overrides a capability refusal: a preference naming a configuration the screen rejected, or one absent from the table, is recorded and refused rather than honoured, and screening stops at that entry instead of sliding to the next -- a card asking for a configuration the instrument cannot use is a card to fix, and quietly granting its second choice hides that. It is not evidence: it raises no grade, supports no number, is not an assumption with a falsifier, and S4 may not cite it.

sample_contrast.description: What this sample offers, as a set. A configuration survives the contrast screen when its requires_contrast is one of these -- membership, not equality. A set because a fluorescent tracer still has refractive-index contrast and so provides both, which is why equality would drop brightfield from a fluorescent question. S3.0 can evaluate this before S3 runs, which none of the priority terms can (4.5.3).
